quotations.quote: This lack of independence will inflate the test statistics, though it won’t bias the observed proportions.

Returns are calculated in excess of the CRSP value-weighted index. For winners that are sold, the average excess return over the following year is 3.4 percent more than it is for losers that are not sold.
For the entire sample PLPA = 0.135 and PGPA = 0.094.
quotations.note: PDF extraction renders equals as 5. t=19, independence caveat in footnote13.

quotations.quote: Assume that our investor’s marginal tax rate is 15 percent and that he has taxable gains against which to offset losses.

Suppose that whichever stock the investor does not sell now, he will sell in one year; ... If he can expect a return of 8 percent on his money ... Using $1,000 as a basis ... the investor’s return is about 4.4 percent higher over the next year if he sells the loser rather than the winner.
